ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: For two parties to deceive or lead each other astray.
EvidenceBody: Frozen-corpus concordance: 207 exact hits in 111 storage files representing 109 independent works. Chan records repeatedly place this ordinary reciprocal act under negation in the assurance, ‘Only provide the assenting heart; we certainly will not deceive one another’ (但辦肯心。必不相賺), with graphic variants in the verb ‘provide’ and the adverb ‘certainly.’ Yuanwu Keqin closes an address with that formula. Dahui Zonggao uses it after answering an interlocutor's request about how to receive and keep a statement. Zhongfeng Mingben quotes the old formula and elsewhere tells a Chan student to trust his words because they will not deceive one another. Puan Yinsu repeats the assurance, but also asks whether an old worthy's saying amounts to mutual deception (古人恁麼道。莫是相賺麼). Affirmative, negative, and interrogative forms retain the same reciprocal act; the Zen-specific bend is the formula's recurring use as a public assurance tied to an assenting heart.
